author: peteswriting
title: One of the early film versions of "Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde" (1920)
text:
The most famous soul-bending story came to life in this silent version. The 1920 silent film adaptation of Robert Louis Stevenson’s 1886 novella, The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde, tells the tale of Dr. Henry Jekyll, a benevolent scientist who runs a poor house. Tempted by his friend, Sir George Carewe, to explore the darker side of life, Jekyll visits a dancing club with loose rules. Carewe believes that to be well-informed, one must invite temptation. This experience leads Jekyll to experiment with chemicals to separate the good and evil sides of humanity into two distinct bodies. However, his alter ego, Mr. Hyde, soon takes over, revealing a deranged and reprobate personality.
Despite its subject matter, the film is a visually appealing black-and-white production, with refined sets that reflect the higher-class society of England at the time. As a silent film, it relies heavily on body language and performance, with minimal titles between scenes–be this unspoken dialogue and narration.
Nevertheless, the action flows smoothly, and the expressionist performances effectively convey the story. John Barrymore’s performance in the title role is exceptional, and his transformation is impressive, with makeup that would have deserved an Oscar if they were awarded at the time.
Every so often, the choral and church-like musical score adds to the film’s religious undertones, enhancing its emotional impact and sense of tragedy. The film’s exploration of good and evil is morally sound, making it a strong contender for the best adaptation of this story.
The film begins by highlighting the dual nature of humanity, with both good and evil sides. It shows how evil can enter a good man’s life through an external personality, reminiscent of the Devil’s temptation in the Garden of Eden.
Dr. Jekyll’s pure-hearted lady companion represents the beautiful side of life, contrasting with the ugliness of evil.
Though the film illustrates that unchecked evil can overtake a person’s character, deciding to turn away from evil and be the good person, with God’s help, is the better plan.
9/10
PETER VEUGELAERS
Released March 18, 1920. Main Cast: Millicent Carewe, John Barrymore, Brandon Hurst. Director John S. Robertson. Clara Beranger writer, Thomas Russell Sullivan writer.
